evidence: CancelOrderUseCase, DeliverOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, PackOrderUseCase, PayOrderUseCase and ShipOrderUseCase all inject OrderLookupService and call this.lookup.getById(orderId); none repeats the not-found handling for orders.

PlaceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and ShipOrderUseCase use the same flow: this.allocations.load(...) → this.reservation.reserve/release/commit(allocations) → this.allocations.persist(allocations) → this.orders.save(order).
The state transitions are delegated to the aggregate: order.pay/pack/ship/deliver/cancel(this.clock.now()), so no status rules are repeated in the use cases.
GetProductStockUseCase.execute checks for a missing product itself with NotFoundError('Product', productId); no product lookup service appears in the material, so this is not a bypass.
ListOrdersUseCase and ListProductStockUseCase are read-only queries that map results through toOrderDto and toProductStockDto, the same DTO mappers the other use cases use.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All ten files are application use cases for the order/inventory workflow. Each one exposes an `execute` entry point and returns DTOs through `toOrderDto` or `toProductStockDto`.

The module uses its own abstractions consistently:
- Every use case that loads a single order goes through `OrderLookupService.getById`. None of them calls `OrderRepository.findById` and handles the not-found case itself.
- Every stock-mutating use case (Place, Cancel, Ship) follows the same order: load allocations through `StockAllocationService.load`, apply the change through `StockReservationService` (reserve/release/commit), then persist.
- The time-stamped state transitions (pay, pack, ship, deliver, cancel) are delegated to the `Order` aggregate methods using `Clock.now()`. The use cases do not repeat the status rules.

`GetProductStockUseCase` does its own `findById` plus `NotFoundError` check for products. Nothing in the material shows a product lookup service it should have used, so this is not a bypass. `ListOrdersUseCase` uses `OrderRepository.findAll`/`findByStatus` directly. That is fine, because `OrderLookupService` only covers single-order lookup. The line-merging logic in `PlaceOrderUseCase.mergeLines` appears only there.

I found no split into unrelated concerns, no duplicated invariant and no bypass of the module's abstractions.
